sla.title: How orders work — time limits & rules
sla.t1b: Accept within 3 minutes. If not, it is cancelled automatically, the customer is refunded and it counts on your shop’s record.
sla.t2b: The pharmacist reviews it within 15 minutes. If not, the order is cancelled and counts on your record.
sla.t3b: Mark it Ready by the time you promised. 10 minutes late — you get a reminder. 30 minutes late — Delivez ops call you. Running behind? Use Delay so the customer and rider see the new time.
sla.t4b: Give the order to the rider only after checking the handover code or scanning the QR.
sla.endH: If an order ends early — who pays
sla.e1: You reject it, miss a time limit, or can’t make it
sla.e1b: Customer gets a full refund. No payment to you. It counts on your shop’s record.
sla.e2: Delivez, the rider or bad weather stops it
sla.e2b: Customer gets a full refund. If you had already started cooking, Delivez pays you for the food.
sla.e3b: Only possible before you accept — nothing lost. After you accept, only Delivez support can cancel; if food was being made, Delivez pays you for it.
sla.e4: Delivery fails at the customer’s door
sla.e4b: Food: Delivez pays you for it. Groceries and medicines: the rider brings them back — check them in as “back on shelf” or “damaged” on the order.
sla.retB: The rider waits 5 minutes while the customer checks. Damaged, wrong or expired items come back to you and are taken off the bill — so pack carefully and check dates.
sla.tip1: Too busy? Set your shop to Busy (or Closed) on the dashboard instead of rejecting orders.
sla.tip2: An item ran out? Mark that item unavailable or offer a substitute — don’t reject the whole order.
sla.tip3: Every ended order shows “Why this order ended” on its page, with any amount Delivez pays you.
